Hedge & Shrub Trimming in Guelph

Cedar hedges, privacy rows and foundation shrubs, shaped cleanly and kept healthy.

Get a Free Quote Call or Text

★★★★★  75+ five-star Google reviews

Hedges and shrubs frame a property — until they start swallowing the front window, crowding the walkway and going bare at the bottom. We shape cedar and privacy hedges, cut back overgrown shrubs and bushes, and clean up every clipping before we leave.

Every weekly mow already includes trimming around obstacles and edging along walkways (trimming & edging). This service is for the hedges and shrubs themselves, as a one-time trim or part of your seasonal maintenance.

The service

Hedges and shrubs, shaped properly

  • Cedar and privacy hedges trimmed straight, square or rounded to your preference
  • Shrubs and bushes cut back from windows, siding, walkways and driveways
  • Hedges shaped slightly wider at the base so light reaches the bottom
  • Clippings raked and blown off lawns, beds and hard surfaces
  • One-time trims, or scheduled with your mowing and cleanups

A hedge cut narrower at the top than the bottom stays green to the ground. Cut the other way, the lower branches lose their light and go thin and bare over a few seasons.

Local know-how

When to trim what in Guelph

Timing matters more than most people think. Spring-flowering shrubs such as lilac and forsythia set next year’s buds soon after they bloom, so they’re trimmed right after flowering — cut them in fall and you cut off next spring’s flowers. Cedar and other evergreen hedges are best trimmed from late spring into summer, once the new growth has come in, with an optional lighter trim later in summer to keep a formal hedge sharp.

Read more

Don’t cut cedars into bare wood. Cedars rarely regrow from old brown wood, so trimming past the green layer can leave holes that never fill. With an overgrown hedge we take it back gradually and tell you honestly how far it can go.

Nesting season. Many birds nest in hedges in spring and early summer, and active nests of migratory birds are protected under federal law. We check hedges before trimming during nesting season and leave a section with an active nest until later.

Late fall. Heavy pruning just before winter leaves fresh cuts exposed to the cold. Light tidying is fine; major shaping waits for the growing season.

Pricing

What affects the price of hedge trimming

Hedge and shrub trimming is quoted per property. The main factors:

  • Length and height of the hedges
  • How overgrown they are since the last trim
  • Number and size of shrubs
  • Ladders or access needed for tall or hard-to-reach sides
Common questions

Hedge trimming questions

How often should a cedar hedge be trimmed?

Once a year keeps most hedges in shape, usually late spring into summer. Twice a year — late spring and again later in summer — keeps a formal hedge sharp.

Can you cut back a badly overgrown hedge?

Usually, in stages. We can take a lot off the sides and top, but cedars don’t regrow from bare brown wood, so cutting past the green layer can leave permanent holes. We’ll tell you how far it can safely go.

When should flowering shrubs be trimmed?

Spring bloomers like lilac and forsythia are trimmed right after they flower. Trimming them in fall removes next spring’s flower buds.

What about bird nests in my hedge?

Active nests of migratory birds are protected under federal law. During nesting season we check before trimming and leave any section with an active nest until the young have left.

Do you clean up the clippings?

Yes. Clippings are raked and blown off your lawn, beds, driveway and walkways before we leave.

Is this the same as trimming and edging?

No. Trimming and edging — around obstacles, along walkways and bed edges — is part of every weekly mow. Hedge and shrub trimming is the hedges and shrubs themselves.
